messages.subject: Simple hierarchical model trouble
parts:
I thought I understood how to implement hierarchical models, but I encounter an unexpected error in even the simplest model I could think of:

    data {
        int N; \\ number of units of observation
        int L; \\ number of total samples
        int unit[L]; \\ index vector specifying the unit of observation
        vector[L] y; \\ vector of sample values
    }
    parameters {
        real muPopMean;
    }
    model {
        vector[N] mu;
        vector[L] thisMu;
        for(n in 1:N){
            mu[n] ~ normal(muPopMean,1);
        }
        for(i in 1:L){
            thisMu[i] <- mu[unit[i]];
        }
        y ~ normal(thisMu,1);
    }


The error message is:

    Error : Error in function stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is nan:0, but must not be nan!
    error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done


Any ideas on what I've neglected this time? Adding print statements here and there seems to pin the error down to the first call to normal(), where I'm sampling a mu value for each unit of observation.

Thanks,

Mike

parts:
On Saturday, July 20, 2013 12:04:49 AM UTC-4, Mike Lawrence wrote:
    model {
        vector[N] mu;
        vector[L] thisMu;
        for(n in 1:N){
            mu[n] ~ normal(muPopMean,1);
        }

mu[n] is accessed before it is defined by putting some number into it. Did you mean for mu to be a parameter or transformed parameter?

Ben
